chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever does not fast during the month of Dhu al-Hijjah until the crescent of Muharram is sighted, upon him is the blood of a sheep, and he has no fast, and he must slaughter [a sheep] at Mina."
If he died and had not fasted these three days, then it is upon his guardian to fulfill it on his behalf. He narrated that.

key_terms.الْوَلِيُّ: Guardian (the person responsible for fulfilling obligations on behalf of the deceased)
key_terms.بِمِنًى: At Mina (the location near Mecca where the sacrifice occurs)
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: Blood of a sheep (a specific sacrificial penalty)
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhu al-Hijjah (the 12th month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.هُلَالُ الْمُحَرَّمِ: Crescent of Muharram (marking the end of the fasting period for pilgrims)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim who does not fast the days of Tashriq in Mina?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* specifies that the penalty for breaking the fast during the Days of Tashriq is the slaughter of a sheep at Mina, reflecting the specific juristic view that the fast is recommended but not obligatory. It further clarifies the mechanism of *qada* (making up) for those who die before fulfilling this duty, assigning the responsibility to the heir. This ruling highlights the distinct Shia perspective on the status of the Days of Tashriq fast compared to other schools of thought.
